arxiv_train_08888.name: @xmath0-connected graph

arxiv_train_08888.name: orientable cycle double cover
arxiv_train_08888.description: A covering of a graph's edges by cycles such that each edge is traversed exactly twice in opposite directions, and the cycles collectively form an orientable surface embedding, deduced for @xmath0-edge-connected projective-planar graphs.

arxiv_train_15474.name: Quantum Liouville Theory
arxiv_train_15474.description: The quantum extension of Liouville CFT, pivotal in string theory and quantum gravity for modeling non-rational conformal field theories with continuous spectra of critical exponents.

arxiv_train_15489.name: co-detection patterns
arxiv_train_15489.description: Observable, interpretable behaviors where agents simultaneously detect related objects, demonstrating effective utilization of contextual information.

arxiv_train_15524.name: Vlasov dynamics
arxiv_train_15524.description: The study of nonlinear wave-particle interactions in collisionless or weakly collisional plasmas, leading to phase-space structures and chirping phenomena.

arxiv_train_15524.name: Krook-like collisions

arxiv_train_15524.name: Relaxation oscillations

arxiv_train_15524.name: Self-trapped vortices in phase-space

arxiv_train_15524.name: Linear dissipation term
arxiv_train_15524.description: A linear approximation in the field equation used to derive simple expressions for hole growth rates and initial perturbation thresholds, consistent with numerical simulations.

arxiv_train_15528.name: Cahn-Hilliard equation

arxiv_train_15528.name: Cahn-Hilliard equation coupled with entropy
arxiv_train_15528.description: An extension of the Cahn-Hilliard model incorporating thermodynamic entropy to capture more complex transition behaviors.

arxiv_train_15528.name: Dynamic transition theory for nonlinear systems

arxiv_train_15528.name: New classification scheme for dynamic transitions
arxiv_train_15528.description: A recently developed systematic approach introduced by the authors to categorize dynamic phase transitions based on underlying physical mechanisms.

arxiv_train_15548.name: line map

arxiv_train_15548.name: poor diffusion
arxiv_train_15548.description: Insufficient spreading of plaintext changes across the ciphertext, leading to weak resistance against differential analysis.

arxiv_train_15585.name: Machine Learning model regression

arxiv_train_15585.name: DIDI positioning team data

arxiv_train_15585.name: Pseudo-migration AP elimination

arxiv_train_15585.name: Fingerprint cluster identification

arxiv_train_15591.name: completely positive linear map
arxiv_train_15591.description: The mathematical construct sought to transform one set of quantum states into another while preserving positivity and complete positivity.

arxiv_train_15591.name: douglas-rachford reflection method

arxiv_train_15591.name: semidefinite feasibility problem

arxiv_train_15592.name: Quartic polynomials @xmath3 and @xmath4

arxiv_train_15592.name: R. Debever, N. Kamran, R. Mclenaghan result
arxiv_train_15592.description: A relativistic classification result serving as the basis for the Riemannian analogue presented in this paper.

arxiv_train_15592.name: Self-dual Einstein Hermitian @xmath0-manifolds
arxiv_train_15592.description: Classification of self-dual Einstein Hermitian @xmath0-manifolds independently achieved by R. Bryant and the first and third authors, extending to ambitoric structures.

arxiv_train_15592.name: Extremal Kähler metrics on toric @xmath0-orbifolds
arxiv_train_15592.description: Future global examples aimed at resolving the existence problem for extremal Kähler metrics on toric @xmath0-orbifolds with additional constraints.

arxiv_train_15599.name: regression analysis

arxiv_train_15599.name: compositional data
arxiv_train_15599.description: Data where components are proportions that sum to a constant, central to the prediction tasks examined in the paper.

arxiv_train_15599.name: data based power transformation
arxiv_train_15599.description: A preprocessing technique applied to compositional data to improve prediction accuracy by handling zero values and stabilizing variance.

arxiv_train_15599.name: standard log-ratio approach
arxiv_train_15599.description: The conventional method for dealing with compositional data in regression, used as a benchmark against the proposed power transformation technique.

arxiv_train_15599.name: principal component regression
arxiv_train_15599.description: A dimensionality reduction technique applied within the regression framework to enhance model performance on compositional predictors.

arxiv_train_15621.name: homogenization method
arxiv_train_15621.description: A technique for deriving effective macroscopic properties of heterogeneous materials by averaging microscopic variations, illustrated using wave and diffusion equations with periodic coefficients.

arxiv_train_15621.name: wave equation
arxiv_train_15621.description: A partial differential equation describing the propagation of waves through a medium, used as an example to demonstrate homogenization in spatially periodic systems.

arxiv_train_15621.name: diffusion equation
arxiv_train_15621.description: A partial differential equation modeling the distribution of a substance within a medium over time, employed alongside the wave equation to showcase homogenization with periodic coefficients.

arxiv_train_15621.name: vibrodynamics approach
arxiv_train_15621.description: An analytical framework from vibrodynamics utilized to present the homogenization method, emphasizing its application to periodic spatial variations in physical systems.

arxiv_train_15623.name: point searching in basic semialgebraic sets
arxiv_train_15623.description: The problem of locating points within basic semialgebraic sets, which is addressed using arithmetic operations proportional to the number of variables and constraints.

arxiv_train_15623.name: @xmath0 arithmetic operations
arxiv_train_15623.description: A computational method involving a specific count of arithmetic operations dependent on the numbers of variables (@xmath1), constraints (@xmath2), and polynomial degree (@xmath3).

arxiv_train_15623.name: intrinsic system degree
arxiv_train_15623.description: A measure of intrinsic complexity for the problems, reaching a worst-case order of @xmath4 based on the problem's characteristics.

arxiv_train_15623.name: non-uniform deterministic algorithms
arxiv_train_15623.description: Algorithms designed to solve the problems deterministically with quasi-polynomial complexity relative to intrinsic parameters.

arxiv_train_15623.name: uniform probabilistic algorithms
arxiv_train_15623.description: Probabilistic algorithms that uniformly address the problems with quasi-polynomial complexity in the worst-case scenario.

arxiv_train_15623.name: polynomial optimization
arxiv_train_15623.description: The overarching field of study focused on finding globally minimal points for polynomial constraints, central to this paper's analysis.

arxiv_train_15623.name: @xmath5 intrinsic complexity
arxiv_train_15623.description: A parameter (@xmath5) quantifying the inherent difficulty of solving polynomial optimization problems based on their structural properties.

arxiv_train_15627.name: controlled growth-like morphing of 2D sheets into 3D shapes
arxiv_train_15627.description: The core technique demonstrated in the paper, involving geometric composite structures that deform by residual swelling to achieve desired 3D shapes from 2D sheets.

arxiv_train_15627.name: residual swelling
arxiv_train_15627.description: The mechanism by which diffusion-driven swelling interacts with geometric confinement to dictate the deformed shape of thin, soft objects.

arxiv_train_15627.name: analytical model for Gaussian and mean curvatures
arxiv_train_15627.description: A theoretical framework presented in the paper that quantitatively describes how geometry, mechanics, and swelling influence the curvature of a thin disk.

arxiv_train_15627.name: competition between two characteristic diffusive length scales
arxiv_train_15627.description: The key dynamic governing the residual swelling process, determined by geometric factors that control the diffusion-driven actuation.

arxiv_train_15627.name: 2D analog of Timoshenko's classical formula for thermal bending of bimetallic beams
arxiv_train_15627.description: A generalization of a classical mechanical formula applied to 2D geometric composites, explaining the influence of geometry and elasticity on Gaussian curvature.

arxiv_train_15627.name: controlled shaping of geometric composites
arxiv_train_15627.description: The proposed approach that leverages the interplay of geometry and material properties to achieve precise shape control as an alternative or complement to traditional manufacturing techniques.

arxiv_train_15633.name: thermal activation model
arxiv_train_15633.description: A theoretical framework used to explain the training and recovery behaviors of exchange bias in spin valves through thermal activation processes.

arxiv_train_15633.name: exchange bias
arxiv_train_15633.description: The shift in the hysteresis loop of a ferromagnet/antiferromagnet bilayer caused by interfacial coupling, which is investigated in feni/Cu/Co/Femn spin valves.

arxiv_train_15633.name: training effect
arxiv_train_15633.description: The phenomenon where repeated magnetic field cycling alters the exchange bias, showing a logarithmic dependence on training cycles.

arxiv_train_15633.name: relaxation time of antiferromagnet spins
arxiv_train_15633.description: A measure of how quickly antiferromagnetic spin orientations relax during field sweep rates, calculated as 61.4, 27.6, and 11.5 units for sweep rates of 1000, 2000, and 4000 oe/s, respectively.

arxiv_train_15633.name: field sweep rates
arxiv_train_15633.description: The varying speeds at which magnetic fields are cycled (1000 to 4800 oe/s) used to study the training and recovery dynamics of exchange bias in spin valves.

arxiv_train_15649.name: Barabási-Albert scale-free network (SFN) model
arxiv_train_15649.description: A directed version of the Barabási-Albert model with symmetric preferential attachment, used to generate a scale-free network structure for studying neuronal dynamics.

arxiv_train_15649.name: Izhikevich interneurons
arxiv_train_15649.description: Fast spiking Izhikevich model neurons employed to simulate inhibitory population behavior in the study of synchronized rhythms.

arxiv_train_15649.name: Synaptic inhibition strength (Θ₀)
arxiv_train_15649.description: A parameter controlling the strength of synaptic inhibition, critical for determining synchronization states in the neuronal network.

arxiv_train_15649.name: Noise intensity (Θ₁)

arxiv_train_15649.name: Partial synchronization

arxiv_train_15649.name: Sparse synchronization (Θ₆ = 1)
arxiv_train_15649.description: A specific form of partial synchronization characterized by intermittent neuronal discharges and degree-dependent mean firing rates.

arxiv_train_15649.name: Order parameter

arxiv_train_15657.name: Fubini-Study metric tensor field

arxiv_train_15657.name: Local Unitary Groups
arxiv_train_15657.description: Groups of transformations acting on quantum states that preserve certain properties, central to the invariance analysis in this study.

arxiv_train_15657.name: Entanglement monotone candidates
arxiv_train_15657.description: Potential measures of entanglement identified through an algorithmic procedure based on invariant functions derived from the Fubini-Study metric.

arxiv_train_15657.name: Quantum version of the Fisher information metric
arxiv_train_15657.description: A quantum analogue of the classical Fisher information metric linked to the Fubini-Study metric, providing a framework for information-theoretic analysis in quantum states.

arxiv_train_15677.name: surface code
arxiv_train_15677.description: A quantum error correction code that is promising for fault-tolerant quantum computation in this paper.

arxiv_train_15677.name: fault-tolerant decoder
arxiv_train_15677.description: An algorithm that computes operations to correct errors based on measured syndromes, even with error-prone measurements, central to the error correction process discussed.

arxiv_train_15677.name: minimum-weight perfect matching
arxiv_train_15677.description: A previously studied decoding technique for qubit codes that lacks generalizability to qudit codes, mentioned as a prior approach in comparison.

arxiv_train_15677.name: Bravyi and Haah decoder
arxiv_train_15677.description: The original fault-tolerant decoder introduced by Bravyi and Haah (2013) generalized for qubits and qudits of any dimension in this work.

arxiv_train_15677.name: generalized uncorrelated bit-flip noise
arxiv_train_15677.description: A noise model applied to both physical qudits and syndrome measurements, used to evaluate decoder performance under higher-dimensional error conditions.

arxiv_train_15677.name: >0% error rate threshold
arxiv_train_15677.description: The achievable error rate threshold exceeding @xmath0%, indicating robustness of the enhanced decoder with high qudit dimensions.

arxiv_train_15681.name: multi-layered feed-forward network with back propagation
arxiv_train_15681.description: The architecture used for supervised learning, consisting of multiple layers connected by weights adjusted via the backpropagation algorithm.

arxiv_train_15681.name: small-world connectivity
arxiv_train_15681.description: A network topology characterized by short average path lengths and high clustering, shown to improve learning efficiency in this study.

arxiv_train_15681.name: regular or random connectivity
arxiv_train_15681.description: Comparison network topologies used as baselines to evaluate the performance of small-world connectivity.

arxiv_train_15681.name: learning error
arxiv_train_15681.description: The quantitative measure of how far the model's predictions deviate from the true labels, reduced by small-world connectivity in this research.

arxiv_train_15681.name: learning time
arxiv_train_15681.description: The duration required for the neural network to converge during training, shortened with small-world connectivity compared to regular/random networks.

arxiv_train_15681.name: data-mining
arxiv_train_15681.description: One of the potential application domains where the findings on improved learning efficiency could be leveraged.

arxiv_train_15681.name: image processing
arxiv_train_15681.description: Another domain identified as benefiting from the reduced learning error and time due to small-world connectivity in neural networks.

arxiv_train_15681.name: speech recognition
arxiv_train_15681.description: A third application area suggested by the authors for utilizing the enhanced learning performance of small-world connected networks.

arxiv_train_15697.name: Bures metric tensor
arxiv_train_15697.description: The geometric measure of distinguishability between quantum states used to analyze three-level quantum systems in this study.

arxiv_train_15697.name: Euler angle-based parameterization

arxiv_train_15697.name: Density matrices

arxiv_train_15697.name: Three-level quantum systems / spin-1 systems

arxiv_train_15698.name: power law

arxiv_train_15698.name: @xmath2

arxiv_train_15698.name: @xmath3
arxiv_train_15698.description: Disorder parameter characterizing the highly dispersive transient currents in time-of-flight experiments, found to be smaller than @xmath4.

arxiv_train_15698.name: @xmath4
arxiv_train_15698.description: Reference value for comparison with the disorder parameter @xmath3 in the context of dispersive transport of charge carriers.

arxiv_train_15698.name: @xmath5
arxiv_train_15698.description: A derived simple relation connecting the geminate recombination rate to the dispersive transport of charge carriers, consistent with measured photoluminescence decay in a-Si:H.

arxiv_train_15702.name: diffusion coefficient

arxiv_train_15702.name: ballistic and diffusive regimes transition
arxiv_train_15702.description: The analysis of the shift from ballistic to diffusive behavior in cosmic ray propagation within varying magnetic field conditions.

arxiv_train_15702.name: magnetic horizon of CR sources

arxiv_train_15702.name: NG magnetic fields

arxiv_train_15706.name: s=1 pseudospin formalism

arxiv_train_15706.name: 2D cuprates model

arxiv_train_15706.name: mixed valence quantum superpositions

arxiv_train_15706.name: correlated one- and two-particle transport

arxiv_train_15722.name: bottom-up hierarchical clustering algorithm

arxiv_train_15722.name: five different distances
arxiv_train_15722.description: Various distance measures compared for their effectiveness in domain clustering within the adaptive MT architecture.

arxiv_train_15722.name: MT benchmark built on 40 commercial domains
arxiv_train_15722.description: A collection of machine translation tasks representing diverse commercial domains used to evaluate the clustering algorithm.

arxiv_train_15722.name: dendrograms
arxiv_train_15722.description: Visual representations of the hierarchical clustering results, showing how domains are grouped at different levels of similarity.

arxiv_train_15722.name: intrinsic and extrinsic evaluations
arxiv_train_15722.description: Methods used to assess the quality of the domain clusters both internally (based on cluster structure) and externally (based on performance metrics).

arxiv_train_15722.name: most expensive distance

arxiv_train_15730.name: side-information scalable (si-scalable) source coding

arxiv_train_15730.name: square error distortion measure

arxiv_train_15730.name: perfectly scalable coding

arxiv_train_15730.name: Wyner-Ziv coding

arxiv_train_15730.name: quadratic Gaussian source with multiple jointly Gaussian side informations

arxiv_train_15742.name: copula

arxiv_train_15742.name: compound process

arxiv_train_15744.name: PPN constraints

arxiv_train_15754.name: GRB 011211

arxiv_train_15834.name: Wiener sheet
